name: ISIC 2024 SLICE-3D: Skin Cancer Detection with 3D-TBP
description: The ISIC 2024 SLICE-3D dataset (Skin Lesion Image Crops Extracted from 3D Total Body Photography) was developed for the ISIC 2024 challenge hosted on Kaggle and MICCAI 2024. Comprising 401,059 standardized lesion image crops (15x15 mm field-of-view) extracted from 3D Total Body Photography (3D-TBP) scans of 2,279 patients across nine international medical centers, SLICE-3D models high-volume, low-prevalence screening environments. Each lesion crop is paired with rich clinical and lesion metadata (anatomical site, patient age, sex, 3D coordinate locations, color/dimension attributes). The primary task is binary classification distinguishing malignant lesions (melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma; ~393 cases) from benign lesions (~400,666 cases) under an extreme class imbalance mimicking clinical primary care screening.
